name: Hilkiah
overview: Hilkiah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Meshullam according to Nehemiah 11:11. His lineage places him within the Levitical family, which historically held priestly and temple duties in Israel. Beyond this unique attribute, no additional notes provide further detail about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Hilkiah means 'YHWH is [my] portion,' reflecting a declaration of dependence on the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a theologically rich meaning consistent with Levitical identity and devotion.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hilkiah as the son of Meshullam, with an inferred relationship to Seraiah as his father. These connections situate him within a known Levitical lineage but do not elaborate further on his family beyond these ties.
scriptureSignificance: Hilkiah's significance in the biblical narrative is grounded in his Levitical heritage, which implies a role connected to the worship and service of God. Being identified as the son of Meshullam in Nehemiah 11:11 places him within the post-exilic community of Israel, contributing to the restoration and maintenance of covenant faithfulness among God's people. Although specific actions are not detailed, his mention affirms the continuity of Levitical service in Israel's history.
